attributes.body:
ごとに is a combination of the noun ごと, and the particle に. Together, they are used adverbially to express that something happens 'every (A)', or 'at intervals of (A)'. ごとに may be used after any verb (usually in non-past form), or noun.

Although ごとに may be used after verbs, the most common use is with nouns, or phrases that finish with nouns.

Caution

ごと is the 訓読（くんよ）み (Japanese reading) of the kanji 毎（まい）, which means 'every'. This fact will be important when trying to remember the difference between ごとに and おきに, a similar grammar point which can also mean 'every', but focuses more on 'interval' or 'gap' of a specific time or distance. Due to おきに focusing on the space between 'each (A)', there are sentences where おきに and ごとに will have different meanings.

Here, we can see that ごとに will mean 'every week', while おきに will mean 'every second week', due to there being a 'one week interval' when おきに is used. To make things easier, these two expressions can be remembered in the following way.

(A) ごとに = During every (A), (B).

(A) おきに = After every space of (A), (B).

Fun Fact

Many native speakers make mistakes with the difference between おきに and ごとに, so there are quite a large number of people (especially in the younger generation) that will consider them completely interchangeable.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: 毎（まい） vs. 毎（ごと）に

attributes.body: Both expressions show frequency, but in different ways. The に (frequency) construction combines a time period with a number to mean '(A) times per (B),' e.g. 一週間に２回 'twice a week'. ごとに attaches to a number + counter to mean 'every X,' e.g. 二時間ごとに薬を飲む 'take medicine every two hours'.

first_relatable.title: に (Frequency)
first_relatable.meaning: Times (In each time period), Every, Frequency of

attributes.body: ごとに and たびに both express frequency, and can be interchangeable in cases like 失敗するたびに／ごとに 'every time (you) fail'. However, ごとに can directly follow time or distance expressions (e.g. ３時間ごとに), while たびに requires a verb indicating an action or event, e.g. ３時間が経つたびに 'every time 3 hours pass'. Their noun forms also differ, e.g. 発表の度に vs. 発表ごとに (both meaning 'with every announcement').

ごとに and たびに both express frequency, but differ in usage. In phrases like 失敗するごとに or 失敗するにつけ 'every time (you fail)', the meaning is similar, though the grammatical attachment is different. につけ is also more formal and literary, while ごとに is common attaches directly to time or distance expressions, e.g. ３時間ごとに 'every 3 hours'.

ごとに and おきに both express regular intervals, but with a key difference. ２日ごとに means 'every two days', i.e. the event happens on the second day. ２日おきに means 'at intervals of two days', or in other words every third day. A helpful tip: おきに comes from 置く, which can have the meaning of leaving a gap or space.

second_relatable.title: おきに
second_relatable.meaning: Repeated at intervals, Every other, Every, At intervals of

attributes.body: Both express regular repetition, but in different structures. ～ずつ attaches to quantity phrases to mean 'each' or 'little by little', e.g. 一つずつください 'Give me one of each.' ごとに follows nouns and means 'every (A)', often time-based, e.g. ３０分ごとに体を動かす 'I move my body every thirty minutes.'

first_relatable.title: ～ずつ
first_relatable.meaning: One at a time, Per, Each, Gradually

attributes.body: Both phrases express frequency but differ in usage. ごとに attaches to time expressions, nouns, or verbs to mean 'every (A),' e.g. ３時間ごとに 'every three hours' or 失敗するごとに 'every time (you) fail'. まい～のように is used only with time words that take 毎 and adds emphasis, meaning 'almost every (A)', e.g. 毎日のように 'nearly every day'.

first_relatable.title: まい～のように
first_relatable.meaning: Almost every ~, Nearly every ~, On a ~ basis
